skill.name: azure-compliance
skill.description: Assess Azure compliance with Azure Quick Review, Azure Resource Graph, and Key Vault expiration checks. The skill helps review security posture, resource configuration, and remediation options for Azure environments.
skill.summary: Audit Azure compliance findings and Key Vault expiration risks.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, Azure MCP tool names, placeholder Azure URLs, and relative documentation links. No prompt-injection text was found, but the skill should limit Key Vault secret retrieval to metadata to avoid exposing secret values.

remediation.issue: Key Vault secret checks may retrieve secret values while only expiration metadata is needed.
remediation.suggestion: Use metadata-only operations or explicit queries that exclude secret values, and redact any secret material from reports.

remediation.issue: Remediation examples include Azure CLI and PowerShell commands that can change cloud resources.
remediation.suggestion: Keep these examples opt-in, require explicit user approval, and document production review steps before execution.

remediation.issue: Live compliance scans can enumerate Azure resources across broad scopes.
remediation.suggestion: Document minimum read permissions and scope each scan to the smallest subscription, resource group, or vault needed.

content.user_title: Audit Azure Compliance and Key Vault Expiration
content.value_statement: Azure teams need clear compliance checks across subscriptions, resource groups, and Key Vault assets. This skill guides azqr scans, Resource Graph review, and prioritized remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides Azure Quick Review scans for subscriptions, resource groups, management groups, and selected services.
Summarizes azqr results by recommendations, impacted resources, inventory, Defender, Advisor, policy, and cost sheets.
Audits Key Vault keys, secrets, and certificates for expired, expiring, missing, and disabled status.
Provides Azure Resource Graph query patterns for tags, public access, HTTPS, roles, and resource locks.
Maps common findings to remediation guidance using Azure CLI, Bicep, and operational recommendations.
Explains Azure authentication patterns for managed identity, local development, and least-privilege RBAC.
limitations: Requires authenticated Azure access and sufficient permissions for the selected scope.
Depends on Azure MCP tools or Azure CLI availability for live scans.
Does not replace formal compliance certification, Azure Policy enforcement, or human risk acceptance.
Remediation examples must be reviewed before changes are applied to production resources.

use_cases.title: Subscription Security Review
use_cases.description: Run an azqr assessment and summarize high-priority Azure security and reliability findings.

use_cases.title: Key Vault Expiration Audit
use_cases.description: Find expired, expiring, disabled, or missing-expiration Key Vault keys, secrets, and certificates.

use_cases.title: Remediation Planning
use_cases.description: Translate compliance findings into prioritized Azure CLI, Bicep, and process-level remediation options.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Compliance Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Azure subscription for compliance issues and summarize the top risks by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Key Vault Expiration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Key Vault for expired items, items expiring within 30 days, and items without expiration dates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Resource Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an Azure compliance review for this production resource group and group findings by security, reliability, cost, and operations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Enterprise Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze azqr results across these scopes, identify recurring control gaps, and create a staged remediation plan with owners and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Check a subscription with azqr and summarize security issues.
output_examples.output: The result is a severity summary, top impacted resources, likely business impact, and prioritized remediation actions.

output_examples.input: Audit Key Vault items expiring in the next 30 days.
output_examples.output: The result groups items as expired, expiring soon, missing expiration, disabled, and healthy, with rotation recommendations.

output_examples.input: Review storage account findings from an azqr report.
output_examples.output: The result explains public access, private endpoint, HTTPS, and soft-delete gaps with safe remediation options.

best_practices: Scope scans to the smallest subscription, resource group, or vault that answers the user request.
Use managed identity and least-privilege RBAC for production access.
Separate reporting from remediation, and require explicit approval before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad tenant-wide scans when a resource-group review is enough.
Do not include secret values, keys, certificates, or tokens in reports.
Do not apply remediation commands to production without review and rollback planning.

faq.question: What Azure tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It references Azure MCP tools, Azure Quick Review, Azure Resource Graph, Azure CLI, and Key Vault SDK patterns.

faq.question: Can it scan all Azure resources?
faq.answer: It focuses on azqr-supported Azure services, Resource Graph queries, and Key Vault expiration checks.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Live scans require Azure authentication and permissions for the target subscription, resource group, or vault.

faq.question: Can it fix compliance issues automatically?
faq.answer: It provides remediation guidance, but production changes should require explicit review and approval.

faq.question: Will it expose Key Vault secrets?
faq.answer: It should inspect metadata only. Secret values should be filtered, redacted, and excluded from reports.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for formal compliance audits?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and triage findings, but formal audit decisions remain with qualified reviewers.
